# Statistical Findings

<!-- Generated by backend/analytics/statistics/findings.py from the official UCI files.
Do not edit by hand. Regenerate: cd backend && python -m analytics.statistics.findings -->

Results of the Phase 4 analysis on the official UCI Student Performance data. All
students are included, including those with G3 = 0. Methods, assumptions and the
correction strategy are described in [METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md#5-statistical-analysis-phase-4).

**How to read this document.**

- Every result is a statistical *association* in observational data from two
  Portuguese schools. None is evidence of cause.
- RQ1–RQ6b are pre-specified confirmatory tests, Holm-adjusted within each cohort.
  Everything else is exploratory.
- Significance does not mean importance: read the effect sizes.
- Confidence intervals are 95% and not adjusted for multiplicity.

## Mathematics (n = 395)

### Final grade (G3)

- Mean 10.42 (95% CI 9.96–10.87), median 11, SD 4.58, IQR 8–14, range 0–20.
- Shape: Left-skewed, near-normal tails (Shapiro–Wilk: normality rejected at α = 0.05). Skewness -0.73, excess kurtosis 0.40.
- Academic risk (G3 < 10): 130 of 395 = 32.9% (95% Wilson CI 28.5–37.7%).
- 38 students (9.6%) have a final grade of 0. They are kept in every analysis and are all at risk by definition.
- 38 of these 38 students have 0 recorded absences, compared with 21.6% of students with G3 > 0. This pattern suggests that some zero grades may reflect a missed final evaluation rather than low attainment; the data cannot confirm this.
- 13 of the 38 also have G2 = 0.

### Research questions

| RQ | Evidence | Test | Adjusted p | Effect | Result |
| -- | -------- | ---- | ---------- | ------ | ------ |
| RQ1 | confirmatory | Spearman correlation | 0.147 | Spearman ρ = 0.11 (weak) | not significant |
| RQ2 | confirmatory | Welch's t-test | < 0.001 | Cohen's d (No past failures − 1 or more) = 0.93 (large) | significant |
| RQ3 | confirmatory | Spearman correlation | 0.880 | Spearman ρ = 0.02 (negligible) | not significant |
| RQ4 | confirmatory | Welch's t-test | 0.147 | Cohen's d (Female − Male) = -0.21 (small) | not significant |
| RQ5 | confirmatory | One-way ANOVA | < 0.001 | η² = 0.05 (small) | significant |
| RQ6a | confirmatory | Welch's t-test | 0.099 | Cohen's d (Yes − No) = -0.25 (small) | not significant |
| RQ6b | confirmatory | Welch's t-test | 0.880 | Cohen's d (Yes − No) = -0.08 (negligible) | not significant |
| RQ7 | exploratory | Spearman correlation matrix | < 0.001 | Spearman ρ (Second period grade) = 0.96 (strong) | significant |
| RQ8 | exploratory | Chi-square test of independence | < 0.001 | Cramér's V (Any past failures) = 0.33 (medium) | significant |

Findings:

- **RQ1.** Weekly study time: no statistically significant association with G3 after correction (ρ = 0.11 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.20), n = 395, Holm-adjusted p = 0.147). This does not show the absence of any relationship; the data are insufficient to reject H0 at α = 0.05.
  *Sensitivity:* Without the 38 students with G3 = 0 (n = 357): ρ = 0.11 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.21), unadjusted p = 0.038. Exploratory sensitivity check only.
- **RQ2.** Any past failures shows a statistically significant association with G3 (Welch's t-test, Cohen's d (No past failures − 1 or more) = 0.93 (95% CI 0.68 to 1.18); No past failures: n = 312, median 11, 1 or more: n = 83, median 8; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Effect size: large. This describes an association in this cohort, not a causal effect.
  *Sensitivity:* Without the 38 students with G3 = 0 (n = 357): Welch's t-test, Cohen's d (No past failures − 1 or more) = 0.76, unadjusted p < 0.001. Exploratory sensitivity check only.
- **RQ3.** School absences: no statistically significant association with G3 after correction (ρ = 0.02 (95% CI -0.08 to 0.12), n = 395, Holm-adjusted p = 0.880). This does not show the absence of any relationship; the data are insufficient to reject H0 at α = 0.05.
  *Sensitivity:* Without the 38 students with G3 = 0 (n = 357): ρ = -0.24 (95% CI -0.34 to -0.14), unadjusted p < 0.001. Exploratory sensitivity check only.
- **RQ4.** Sex: no statistically significant association with G3 after correction (Welch's t-test, Cohen's d (Female − Male) = -0.21 (95% CI -0.41 to -0.01); Female: n = 208, median 10, Male: n = 187, median 11; Holm-adjusted p = 0.147). This does not show the absence of any relationship; the data are insufficient to reject H0 at α = 0.05.
  *Sensitivity:* Without the 38 students with G3 = 0 (n = 357): Welch's t-test, Cohen's d (Female − Male) = -0.21, unadjusted p = 0.053. Exploratory sensitivity check only.
- **RQ5.** Mother's education shows a statistically significant association with G3 (One-way ANOVA, η² = 0.05; Primary or less: n = 62, median 10, 5th to 9th grade: n = 103, median 11, Secondary: n = 99, median 10, Higher education: n = 131, median 12; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Effect size: small. This describes an association in this cohort, not a causal effect.
  *Sensitivity:* Without the 38 students with G3 = 0 (n = 357): Welch's ANOVA, η² = 0.04, unadjusted p = 0.001. Exploratory sensitivity check only.
- **RQ6a.** Extra school support: no statistically significant association with G3 after correction (Welch's t-test, Cohen's d (Yes − No) = -0.25 (95% CI -0.54 to 0.05); Yes: n = 51, median 10, No: n = 344, median 11; Holm-adjusted p = 0.099). This does not show the absence of any relationship; the data are insufficient to reject H0 at α = 0.05.
  *Sensitivity:* Without the 38 students with G3 = 0 (n = 357): Welch's t-test, Cohen's d (Yes − No) = -0.71, unadjusted p < 0.001. Exploratory sensitivity check only.
- **RQ6b.** Family educational support: no statistically significant association with G3 after correction (Welch's t-test, Cohen's d (Yes − No) = -0.08 (95% CI -0.28 to 0.12); Yes: n = 242, median 11, No: n = 153, median 11; Holm-adjusted p = 0.880). This does not show the absence of any relationship; the data are insufficient to reject H0 at α = 0.05.
  *Sensitivity:* Without the 38 students with G3 = 0 (n = 357): Welch's t-test, Cohen's d (Yes − No) = -0.14, unadjusted p = 0.202. Exploratory sensitivity check only.
- **RQ7.** Interim grades are the strongest correlates of G3: Second period grade ρ = 0.96 (BH-adjusted p < 0.001); First period grade ρ = 0.88 (BH-adjusted p < 0.001). Among non-grade variables the strongest are: Past class failures ρ = -0.36 (BH-adjusted p < 0.001); Mother's education ρ = 0.23 (BH-adjusted p < 0.001); Age ρ = -0.17 (BH-adjusted p = 0.003). Rankings are exploratory and describe association only.
- **RQ8.** Associated with academic risk after FDR control: Any past failures (V = 0.33, medium, BH-adjusted p < 0.001); Wants higher education (V = 0.16, small, BH-adjusted p = 0.011). These are exploratory associations.

## Portuguese language (n = 649)

### Final grade (G3)

- Mean 11.91 (95% CI 11.66–12.16), median 12, SD 3.23, IQR 10–14, range 0–19.
- Shape: Left-skewed, heavier-tailed than normal (Shapiro–Wilk: normality rejected at α = 0.05). Skewness -0.91, excess kurtosis 2.71.
- Academic risk (G3 < 10): 100 of 649 = 15.4% (95% Wilson CI 12.8–18.4%).
- 15 students (2.3%) have a final grade of 0. They are kept in every analysis and are all at risk by definition.
- 15 of these 15 students have 0 recorded absences, compared with 36.1% of students with G3 > 0. This pattern suggests that some zero grades may reflect a missed final evaluation rather than low attainment; the data cannot confirm this.
- 7 of the 15 also have G2 = 0.

### Research questions

| RQ | Evidence | Test | Adjusted p | Effect | Result |
| -- | -------- | ---- | ---------- | ------ | ------ |
| RQ1 | confirmatory | Spearman correlation | < 0.001 | Spearman ρ = 0.27 (weak) | significant |
| RQ2 | confirmatory | Mann–Whitney U | < 0.001 | Rank-biserial r (No past failures vs 1 or more) = 0.71 (strong) | significant |
| RQ3 | confirmatory | Spearman correlation | < 0.001 | Spearman ρ = -0.16 (weak) | significant |
| RQ4 | confirmatory | Welch's t-test | 0.003 | Cohen's d (Female − Male) = 0.26 (small) | significant |
| RQ5 | confirmatory | Kruskal–Wallis H | < 0.001 | η²_H (rank-based) = 0.08 (medium) | significant |
| RQ6a | confirmatory | Mann–Whitney U | 0.052 | Rank-biserial r (Yes vs No) = -0.16 (weak) | not significant |
| RQ6b | confirmatory | Mann–Whitney U | 0.455 | Rank-biserial r (Yes vs No) = 0.03 (negligible) | not significant |
| RQ7 | exploratory | Spearman correlation matrix | < 0.001 | Spearman ρ (Second period grade) = 0.94 (strong) | significant |
| RQ8 | exploratory | Chi-square test of independence | < 0.001 | Cramér's V (Any past failures) = 0.40 (medium) | significant |

Findings:

- **RQ1.** Weekly study time shows a statistically significant association with G3 (ρ = 0.27 (95% CI 0.20 to 0.35), n = 649, Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Effect size: weak. This describes an association in this cohort, not a causal effect.
  *Sensitivity:* Without the 15 students with G3 = 0 (n = 634): ρ = 0.26 (95% CI 0.19 to 0.34), unadjusted p < 0.001. Exploratory sensitivity check only.
- **RQ2.** Any past failures shows a statistically significant association with G3 (Mann–Whitney U, Rank-biserial r (No past failures vs 1 or more) = 0.71; No past failures: n = 549, median 12, 1 or more: n = 100, median 10; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Effect size: strong. This describes an association in this cohort, not a causal effect.
  *Sensitivity:* Without the 15 students with G3 = 0 (n = 634): Welch's t-test, Cohen's d (No past failures − 1 or more) = 1.31, unadjusted p < 0.001. Exploratory sensitivity check only.
- **RQ3.** School absences shows a statistically significant association with G3 (ρ = -0.16 (95% CI -0.23 to -0.08), n = 649, Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Effect size: weak. This describes an association in this cohort, not a causal effect.
  *Sensitivity:* Without the 15 students with G3 = 0 (n = 634): ρ = -0.21 (95% CI -0.29 to -0.14), unadjusted p < 0.001. Exploratory sensitivity check only.
- **RQ4.** Sex shows a statistically significant association with G3 (Welch's t-test, Cohen's d (Female − Male) = 0.26 (95% CI 0.11 to 0.42); Female: n = 383, median 12, Male: n = 266, median 11; Holm-adjusted p = 0.003). Effect size: small. This describes an association in this cohort, not a causal effect.
  *Sensitivity:* Without the 15 students with G3 = 0 (n = 634): Welch's t-test, Cohen's d (Female − Male) = 0.27, unadjusted p < 0.001. Exploratory sensitivity check only.
- **RQ5.** Mother's education shows a statistically significant association with G3 (Kruskal–Wallis H, η²_H (rank-based) = 0.08; Primary or less: n = 149, median 11, 5th to 9th grade: n = 186, median 12, Secondary: n = 139, median 12, Higher education: n = 175, median 13; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Effect size: medium. This describes an association in this cohort, not a causal effect.
  *Sensitivity:* Without the 15 students with G3 = 0 (n = 634): Welch's ANOVA, η² = 0.09, unadjusted p < 0.001. Exploratory sensitivity check only.
- **RQ6a.** Extra school support: no statistically significant association with G3 after correction (Mann–Whitney U, Rank-biserial r (Yes vs No) = -0.16; Yes: n = 68, median 11, No: n = 581, median 12; Holm-adjusted p = 0.052). This does not show the absence of any relationship; the data are insufficient to reject H0 at α = 0.05.
  *Sensitivity:* Without the 15 students with G3 = 0 (n = 634): Welch's t-test, Cohen's d (Yes − No) = -0.31, unadjusted p = 0.002. Exploratory sensitivity check only.
- **RQ6b.** Family educational support: no statistically significant association with G3 after correction (Mann–Whitney U, Rank-biserial r (Yes vs No) = 0.03; Yes: n = 398, median 12, No: n = 251, median 12; Holm-adjusted p = 0.455). This does not show the absence of any relationship; the data are insufficient to reject H0 at α = 0.05.
  *Sensitivity:* Without the 15 students with G3 = 0 (n = 634): Welch's t-test, Cohen's d (Yes − No) = -0.01, unadjusted p = 0.928. Exploratory sensitivity check only.
- **RQ7.** Interim grades are the strongest correlates of G3: Second period grade ρ = 0.94 (BH-adjusted p < 0.001); First period grade ρ = 0.88 (BH-adjusted p < 0.001). Among non-grade variables the strongest are: Past class failures ρ = -0.45 (BH-adjusted p < 0.001); Mother's education ρ = 0.28 (BH-adjusted p < 0.001); Weekly study time ρ = 0.27 (BH-adjusted p < 0.001). Rankings are exploratory and describe association only.
- **RQ8.** Associated with academic risk after FDR control: Any past failures (V = 0.40, medium, BH-adjusted p < 0.001); Wants higher education (V = 0.31, medium, BH-adjusted p < 0.001); School (V = 0.30, small, BH-adjusted p < 0.001); Father's education (V = 0.18, small, BH-adjusted p < 0.001); Weekly study time (V = 0.17, small, BH-adjusted p < 0.001); Mother's education (V = 0.16, small, BH-adjusted p = 0.001); Home address type (V = 0.13, small, BH-adjusted p = 0.002); Internet at home (V = 0.09, negligible, BH-adjusted p = 0.040). These are exploratory associations.
